title: PMAY Gramin 2026: Free Pucca House Rs 1.20-1.30 Lakh
meta_description: PMAY-G (former Indira Awas Yojana) gives Rs 1.20-1.30 lakh per pucca house. Check the Bihar beneficiary list and status at pmayg.nic.in. IAY merged into PMAY-G.

hero.one_liner: Government of India's rural housing scheme - assistance to build a pucca (permanent) house for SECC-identified rural poor; 2.92 crore houses completed since 2016

what_is_it: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G) is the Government of India's flagship rural housing scheme, providing financial assistance to economically weaker rural households to construct a pucca (permanent) house with basic amenities. The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.

PMAY-G was launched on 20 November 2016, replacing the Indira Awas Yojana (IAY) which had been running since 1985. The transition aimed to make rural housing more accountable, faster, and digitally tracked - every house under PMAY-G is geo-tagged with photographs at each construction milestone.

Financial assistance under PMAY-G is ₹1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh per house in hilly states, Northeastern states, and Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected areas. As of August 2025, of the cumulative target of 4.12 crore houses (Phase I + Phase II), 3.86 crore beneficiaries have been sanctioned and 2.92 crore houses have been completed.
The scheme has been extended by the Union Cabinet to build an additional 2 crore rural houses from April 2024 to March 2029, taking the total target to 4.95 crore houses.

extra_sections.heading: What PMAY-G Is, and the Indira Awas Connection
content: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Gramin, or PMAY-G, is the central government's rural housing scheme. It gives poor rural families money to build a pucca house.
It was launched on 20 November 2016, replacing the old Indira Awas Yojana that ran from 1985. Most people in villages still search for it as Indira Awas Yojana.
The two names point to the same scheme and the same beneficiary database. That is why a search for the Indira Awas list lands you at the PMAY-G portal.
The scheme runs in rural Gram Panchayat areas only. Urban housing is handled separately under PMAY-Urban.
The aim has stayed the same across both names: a pucca house for every eligible rural family living in a kutcha home or without shelter.

extra_sections.heading: How Much You Get and Where
content: The assistance is Rs 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas. It rises to Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly states, the Northeast, and Left Wing Extremism affected areas.
This is not a loan and there is no repayment. The money is released in stages, each tied to verified construction progress through geo-tagged photos.
Payments go straight to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account. There is no cash handling at any stage.
Each release is verified through geo-tagged photos uploaded by a Block official. This keeps the process transparent and traceable.

extra_sections.title: Scheme extended to March 2029 - 2 crore more houses sanctioned
extra_sections.content: The Union Cabinet has approved continuation of PMAY-G for Phase II - building an additional 2 crore pucca houses from April 2024 to March 2029. The overall cumulative target is now 4.95 crore houses. As of August 2025, 3.86 crore have been sanctioned and 2.92 crore are completed. The Phase II beneficiary list is drawn from the Awaas+ 2018 list (updated) plus the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List.

extra_sections.heading: How PMAY-G Money is Paid
content: The ₹1.20 lakh (₹1.30 lakh for hilly/NE/LWE areas) is not paid as a single lump sum. It is released in installments, linked to construction progress - verified by geo-tagged photographs at each stage:
Installment 1 - On sanction: First installment released to beneficiary's bank account after house is sanctioned and foundation work begins.
Installment 2 - Lintel level: Released after construction reaches the lintel level. Geo-tagged photo proof is uploaded by the Block official via the Awaassoft mobile app.
Installment 3 - Roof completion: Released after roof is laid and verified by geo-tagged photographs.

Final installment - Completed house: Released after the house is fully completed with toilet (Swachh Bharat Mission convergence), kitchen, and other basic amenities. The completed house must be geo-tagged.

Beyond the central PMAY-G assistance, beneficiaries can also avail: (a) ₹12,000 from Swachh Bharat Mission–Gramin for toilet construction, (b) 90-95 person-days of unskilled labour wages under MGNREGA, (c) free electricity connection under Saubhagya Scheme, (d) free LPG connection under PM Ujjwala Yojana, (e) free piped water under Jal Jeevan Mission.
The first instalment lands after the house is sanctioned and the foundation begins. Later instalments follow each verified stage.
Because each release needs a geo-tagged photo, you cannot draw the full amount upfront. Plan your spending around the staged release.

steps.title: Block Verification
steps.desc: Officer verifies eligibility and land status

extra_sections.heading: How Families Are Selected
content: PMAY-G is not first-come-first-served. Selection runs on the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List and the updated Awaas+ 2018 survey list.
The Gram Sabha validates the list at village level, and a Block officer verifies each case. Scheduled caste and tribe families, widows, the elderly, the disabled, and homeless families get priority.
If your name is not on the list, you cannot simply fill a form to be added. You ask your Block Development Officer to include you in the next survey.
Around 15 percent of funds are earmarked for minority families, and there is an effort to keep 3 percent of beneficiaries persons with disabilities.
When two households tie within a group, priority goes to those with a widow, a single girl child, or a member with a serious illness.

extra_sections.heading: Who Qualifies for PMAY-G
qualify: Rural household in any state of India (Gram Panchayat area)
Listed in SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List or Awaas+ 2018 list
Currently houseless OR living in 0-2 room kutcha house
Own the plot of land (or eligible for land assistance)
No member of household already has a pucca house under any government scheme
disqualify: Family already owns a pucca house anywhere in India
Living in an urban area / municipal corporation (apply for PMAY-U instead)
Family member is government employee earning above ₹15,000/month
Family member is a taxpayer (income tax or professional tax)
Family owns kisan credit card with credit limit ₹50,000 or above
Household member owns motorised 4-wheeler or fishing boat

extra_sections.heading: Land and Common Delays
content: You must own the plot or hold a valid title to build on it. Land that is still in a deceased parent's name needs a succession certificate first.
Some states give landless families a small plot under a land-assistance component. Check this with your Block office if you have no land.
Delays most often come from land title gaps, an Aadhaar not seeded to the bank, or a name mismatch across documents.
Uploading clear scans and matching every detail to your Aadhaar reduces the chance of a held-up application.

extra_sections.title: Check Land Title Before You Start
extra_sections.content:
Confirm the plot is in your name with a clear title before construction begins. A title in a deceased relative's name needs a succession certificate first.

Sorting this early avoids the most common cause of stalled PMAY-G cases.

extra_sections.heading: Benefits You Can Stack With PMAY-G
content: A PMAY-G house is meant to come with basic amenities, not just walls. You can converge several other schemes alongside it.
These include a toilet grant under Swachh Bharat, labour wages under MGNREGA, a free electricity connection, an LPG connection under Ujjwala, and piped water under Jal Jeevan Mission.
Under MGNREGA a beneficiary can claim about 90 to 95 days of unskilled labour wages for the construction. This eases the cost of building.
A separate toilet grant of Rs 12,000 comes through Swachh Bharat. Together these make the house liveable, not just built.

extra_sections.heading: Phase II: Two Crore More Houses
content: The scheme was extended into Phase II, from April 2024 to March 2029, with two crore more houses sanctioned. The cumulative target is now about 4.95 crore houses.
As of August 2025, around 3.86 crore had been sanctioned and 2.92 crore completed. The Phase II list draws from the updated Awaas+ and SECC databases.
The original Phase I deadline was March 2024 for the first set of houses. Phase II then carried the target forward to March 2029.
This makes PMAY-G one of the largest housing programmes in the world by sheer scale. The numbers run into crores of completed homes.

extra_sections.title: PMAY-G houses completed since 2016
extra_sections.desc: Of the cumulative target of 4.12 crore (Phase I + Phase II), 3.86 crore have been sanctioned and 2.92 crore have been completed (as of August 2025). With Phase II extension to March 2029, the total target is now 4.95 crore rural pucca houses - making PMAY-G one of the world's largest housing programmes by scale.

extra_sections.heading: Common Reasons for PMAY-G Rejection or Delay
content: PMAY-G applications and disbursements get delayed or rejected for these specific reasons. Watch for these:
1. Not in SECC / Awaas+ list.
PMAY-G selection is NOT first-come-first-served. You must be on the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List or Awaas+ 2018 list.
If you are not listed, contact your Block Development Officer to apply for inclusion in the upcoming survey.
2. Land title issues.
You must own the plot or have a legal title. If the land is in your father's name (deceased), get a succession certificate first.
3. Already a pucca house in family.
If any family member owns a pucca house anywhere in India, the family is disqualified.
4. Disqualifying assets.
Owning a 4-wheeler, kisan credit card with limit ₹50,000+, or being a government employee earning ₹15,000+/month all disqualify the household.
5. Aadhaar-bank mismatch.
The beneficiary's Aadhaar must be linked to bank account and NPCI-mapped. Otherwise installment transfers silently fail.
6. Construction stalled or geo-tagging incomplete.
Each milestone needs geo-tagged photo upload by Block official. If construction stalls or the geo-tag is not uploaded, the next installment is held.
A name that is missing from the list is not always a rejection. It can simply mean the verification or survey for your case is still pending.
If the delay drags on, an RTI to the Block office asking the reason for a reverted or inactive status often gets things moving.

extra_sections.heading: Why Bihar Searches for Indira Awas
content: Bihar has one of the largest rural populations waiting for pucca housing. Families there grew up with the Indira Awas name and still use it.
So in Bihar the common searches are for the Indira Awas list, the panchayat list, and instalment status. All of these are now served by the PMAY-G portal at pmayg.nic.in.
In 2026, Bihar has begun AI-based verification that removes ineligible names from the list. A missing name can mean pending verification rather than rejection, so it is worth checking the reason.
The Bihar list is organised by district, block, and panchayat. You drill down to your village to find your name.
Instalments in Bihar are released as construction reaches each stage. Verification and survey work that had slowed earlier has resumed across districts.
Under the new 2026 rules, a family earning up to about Rs 15,000 a month, even owning a two-wheeler, can still be considered. The deprivation criteria were widened.
Always confirm your status on the official portal rather than trusting a middleman. The check is free and takes a few minutes.
Bihar's rural housing demand remains among the highest in the country, which is why these searches stay so common year after year.

States must complete pending approvals by 30 June 2026

extra_sections.heading: Indira Awas Yojana Bihar: List and Status
content: In Bihar, the scheme people still call Indira Awas Yojana is the same as PMAY-Gramin. The old name stuck, so many in rural Bihar search for the Indira Awas list rather than PMAY-G.
Selection in Bihar runs on SECC 2011 deprivation data, verified by the Gram Sabha. Scheduled caste and tribe families, widows, the elderly, the disabled, and homeless families get priority.

Bihar beneficiaries get Rs 1.20 lakh in the plains, paid in instalments tied to construction stages, straight to an Aadhaar-linked account. In 2026, AI-based verification is removing ineligible names from the list.

extra_sections.heading: How to Check the Indira Awas Bihar List

steps.title: Open pmayg.nic.in
steps.desc: Go to the official PMAY-G portal at pmayg.nic.in. The old iay.nic.in address now redirects here.

steps.title: Open IAY/PMAYG Beneficiary
steps.desc: Under the Stakeholders menu, click IAY/PMAYG Beneficiary. The IAY label is kept so legacy applicants can still find old records.

steps.title: Search by number or name
steps.desc: Enter your registration number, or use Advanced Search and pick Bihar, your district, block, and panchayat, then enter your name.

steps.title: Read your status
steps.desc: The record shows sanction status and instalment details. A missing name may mean pending verification, not rejection.

extra_sections.heading: There Is No Direct Application Form
content: PMAY-G has no open application form for citizens to fill on their own. This surprises many first-time applicants.
You become eligible only by being on the SECC or Awaas+ survey list. The Gram Sabha then takes up your case.
So the real first step is to confirm whether your household is on the list. If not, the route is the Block Development Office, not an online form.
The Awaas+ self-survey is the route to update your details to current standards. Your Block office can guide you through it.
Keep your Aadhaar, ration card, and bank passbook ready, since these are checked during verification.

extra_sections.title: You Cannot Self-Apply Online
extra_sections.desc:
PMAY-G selection is survey-based, not form-based. You must be on the SECC 2011 or Awaas+ 2018 list to be considered.

If you are not listed, ask your Block Development Officer to include you in the next survey, rather than paying any agent.

extra_sections.heading: Avoiding Scams and Getting Help
content: No agent can add your name to a PMAY-G list. Only the Gram Sabha and Block officials can, based on the survey databases.
If anyone demands money to get you a house, it is a scam. Report it at your Block Development Office or the helpline 1800-11-6446.

extra_sections.title: Do not pay anyone to get listed in PMAY-G
extra_sections.content: PMAY-G beneficiary lists are drawn from the SECC 2011 and Awaas+ 2018 survey databases. No agent or middleman can "add your name" - only the Gram Sabha and Block officials can. If anyone asks for ₹5,000-₹50,000 to "get you a PMAY-G house," it is a scam. Approach your Block Development Office or call the helpline 1800-11-6446 to report it.

how_to_apply.title: Check if you are in the SECC / Awaas+ list
how_to_apply.description: PMAY-G has no separate application form for direct citizens. You must be on the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List or Awaas+ 2018 list. Visit pmayg.nic.in or your Gram Panchayat office to check. If you are not on the list but believe you qualify, apply for inclusion via the next Awaas+ survey through your Block Development Office.

how_to_apply.title: Gram Sabha selection
how_to_apply.description: Eligible households from the SECC/Awaas+ list are taken up by the Gram Sabha (village council). The Gram Sabha approves the priority list based on need (houselessness, kutcha house condition, vulnerability). Approved names go to the Block office for verification.

how_to_apply.title: Block verification and sanction
how_to_apply.description: Block Development Officer verifies your eligibility (current housing status, land title, Aadhaar-bank linkage). Once verified, the house is sanctioned and you appear in the PMAY-G beneficiary list. You will receive a unique PMAY-G ID.

how_to_apply.title: Begin construction and receive installments
how_to_apply.description: Start construction on your land. The first installment is released as soon as work begins (foundation). Subsequent installments come at lintel, roof, and completion stages - each verified by geo-tagged photographs via the Awaassoft mobile app. The full ₹1.20 lakh (₹1.30 lakh for hilly/NE) is released over 6-12 months from sanction. Apply for convergent benefits (toilet, LPG, water) simultaneously.

important_alert.text: PMAY-G beneficiary selection is from SECC 2011 / Awaas+ 2018 lists - there is no first-come-first-served application. Phase II extended to March 2029 with 2 crore additional houses sanctioned.

faqs.question: How much money is given under PMAY-G?
faqs.answer: PMAY-G provides ₹1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh per house in hilly states, North-Eastern states, and Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected areas. This is released in 3-4 installments tied to construction milestones - foundation, lintel level, roof completion, and final completion - each verified by geo-tagged photographs via the Awaassoft app.

faqs.question: How can I apply for PMAY-G online?
faqs.answer:
PMAY-G does not have a direct online application form for citizens. Selection is from the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List and Awaas+ 2018 list.

To check if you are listed, visit pmayg.nic.in or your Gram Panchayat office. If you are not listed but believe you qualify, request inclusion in the next Awaas+ survey through your Block Development Office.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for PMAY-G in 2026?
faqs.answer: Eligibility requires: (1) rural household in any state, (2) listed in SECC 2011 PWL or Awaas+ 2018 list, (3) currently houseless or living in 0-2 room kutcha house, (4) family does not own a pucca house anywhere in India. Disqualifying factors include: family member is a taxpayer, government employee earning ₹15,000+/month, owns a 4-wheeler, or has a kisan credit card with limit ₹50,000+.

faqs.question: How is PMAY-G different from PMAY-U?
faqs.answer:
PMAY-Gramin (PMAY-G) is for rural areas - administered by the Ministry of Rural Development. It provides ₹1.20-1.30 lakh per house as direct assistance to build a house on your own land.

PMAY-Urban (PMAY-U) is for urban areas - administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. It offers four verticals including interest subsidy under CLSS, beneficiary-led construction, affordable housing in partnership, and in-situ slum redevelopment.

faqs.question: What was the Indira Awas Yojana (IAY)?
faqs.answer:
Indira Awas Yojana (IAY) was the predecessor rural housing scheme of the Government of India, running from 1985 to 2016. On 20 November 2016, IAY was restructured and renamed as Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G).

The new scheme added geo-tagging, digital tracking, time-bound milestones, and convergence with toilet, electricity, LPG, and water schemes - addressing the slow execution problems of IAY.

faqs.question: Can I get a PMAY-G house if I am landless?
faqs.answer:
Yes. As of August 2025, 2,68,480 landless families have been approved for housing under PMAY-G.

Landless beneficiaries are assisted with land allotment by the state government, typically through Gram Sabha-approved community plots or surplus government land. The construction assistance (₹1.20-1.30 lakh) is then given to build on that allotted land.

faqs.question: Can the PMAY-G house be in the woman's name?
faqs.answer:
Yes, and this is strongly encouraged. As of recent data, nearly 75% of houses sanctioned under PMAY-G are either registered in the woman's name or under joint ownership with her husband.

This is a deliberate policy choice to strengthen women's social and financial security in rural areas. Households are encouraged to register the house in the wife's name.

faqs.question: What additional benefits come with PMAY-G?
faqs.answer: PMAY-G is linked with convergent benefits: (1) ₹12,000 for an in-house toilet under Swachh Bharat Mission – Gramin, (2) 90-95 person-days of unskilled labour wages under MGNREGA for construction work, (3) free electricity connection under Saubhagya Scheme, (4) free LPG connection under PM Ujjwala Yojana, (5) free piped water connection under Jal Jeevan Mission, (6) insurance under PMSBY (accident) and PMJJBY (life). Apply for these simultaneously with PMAY-G.

faqs.question: How do I check the Indira Awas Yojana Bihar list?
faqs.answer:
Indira Awas Yojana in Bihar is now PMAY-Gramin. Check the list at pmayg.nic.in under Stakeholders, then IAY/PMAYG Beneficiary.

Use your registration number, or Advanced Search by selecting Bihar, your district, block, and panchayat. The record shows your sanction and instalment status.
